question.problem:
An economist measured $4$ particular features, ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4},$ for each currency in a collection under devaluation. The collected data was stored in the standardized observation matrix $X,$ where each row contains measurements for a particular currency.
The singular values of $X$ are 

$$
{\sigma }_{1}=12,\,{\sigma }_{2}=7,\,{\sigma }_{3}=3,\,{\sigma }_{4}=1.
$$

The economist then converted the original observation matrix $X$ into a new matrix $Y$ using the equation $Y=X{V}_{1},$ where ${V}_{1}$ is the $4\times 1$ matrix consisting of the first principal component of the data. What percentage of the original variance is preserved in the new transformed matrix $Y$ compared to the initial observation matrix $X?$
question.worked_solution:
Let $V$ be the matrix of principal components. Then, applying the change of variables

$$
Y=XV
$$

we can convert our observation matrix $X$ into a new matrix $Y$ of (linearly) transformed observations such that

- the covariance matrix of $Y$ is diagonal (meaning that the new features ${y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{4}$ are uncorrelated),

- the features ${y}_{1},{y}_{2},{y}_{3},{y}_{4}$ are arranged in order of decreasing variance, and

- the squares of the singular values ${\sigma }_{1}^{2},{\sigma }_{2}^{2},{\sigma }_{3}^{2},{\sigma }_{4}^{2}$ represent the variances in the respective features ${y}_{1},{y}_{2},{y}_{3},{y}_{4}.$

Now, the total variance over all features is proportional to the sum of the squared singular values:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Total} & ∝{\sum }_{i=1}^{4}{\sigma }_{i}^{2} \\  & =(12)^{2}+(7)^{2}+(3)^{2}+(1)^{2} \\  & =203\end{aligned}
$$

Since the economist used only the first principal component, the remaining variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Remaining} & ∝{\sum }_{i=1}^{1}{\sigma }_{i}^{2} \\  & =(12)^{2} \\  & =144.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our required percentage can be computed as

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{Remaining}}{\text{Total}} & =\frac{144}{203} \\  & ≈0.709 \\  & =70.9%.\end{aligned}
$$
